settings.title: AI Diagnostic Demo
settings.heading: Which AI exam are you ready for?
settings.intro: A 12-question sample of the AI certification diagnostic. The full version has 45 questions; these sample questions are public, so their answers are shown after you submit.

FND.name: AI & Machine Learning Foundations
FND.study: Know the ML task types: classification, regression, clustering, reinforcement learning, supervised vs. unsupervised. Also know when generative AI fits better than predictive AI or a search engine.
FND.objectives: GAI 1.1 · AI-901 Identify AI workloads · ITS 1.1–1.2

GEN.name: How Generative AI Works
GEN.study: Tokens, embeddings, LLMs vs. diffusion models; what training requires (data, GPUs, energy); model parameters such as temperature and max tokens.
GEN.objectives: GAI 1.1–1.2 · AI-901 Identify AI model components and configurations

PRM.name: Prompt Engineering & Refinement
PRM.study: Zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, self-consistency, generate knowledge, prompt chaining, reverse prompting. Improve prompts with content, style, persona and context; know what system prompts do.
PRM.objectives: GAI 3.1–3.4 · AI-901 Create effective system and user prompts

CRT.name: Creating & Transforming Content
CRT.study: Choosing prompts for text, image and video tasks (summarize, reformat, translate, subtitle, avatar, colorize) and choosing a tool (privacy, cost, licensing, output control).

VER.name: Verifying Output & Limitations
VER.study: Hallucinations, inconsistency, outdated knowledge; how to verify historical facts, current facts and numerical data against reliable sources.

ETH.name: Responsible AI, Ethics, Law & Privacy
ETH.study: Microsoft's six Responsible AI principles; sources of bias; intellectual property; PII and data privacy; who is accountable for AI output.

AZR.name: Azure AI Services & Microsoft Foundry
AZR.study: Vision (object detection, OCR), Azure AI Language, Azure Speech, Content Understanding, grounding/RAG, and agents in Microsoft Foundry.
AZR.objectives: AI-901 Identify AI workloads; Implement AI solutions using Microsoft Foundry

DAT.name: Data Collection & Preparation
DAT.study: Data quality issues (missing values, outliers, invalid entries), encoding categorical data, text features (bag-of-words, TF-IDF), train/test splits, stratification.

MOD.name: Model Training & Evaluation
MOD.study: Overfitting vs. underfitting, ways to prevent overfitting, classification metrics (precision, recall, F1) vs. regression metrics (MAE, RMSE).

OPS.name: Deployment, Monitoring & Lifecycle
OPS.study: Data drift vs. concept drift, logging and monitoring, retraining triggers, documentation, change control and scope creep.

items.stem: A bank wants a model to label each credit card transaction as “fraud” or “not fraud.” What type of machine learning task is this?
items.why: Choosing between fixed categories is classification. Regression predicts a number.

items.stem: In a generative AI model's settings, what does “max tokens” control?
options: How many people can use the model at once
The maximum length of the model's response
How much data the model was trained on
items.why: Max tokens caps how long a response can be. Temperature, not max tokens, controls how random or creative it is.

items.stem: Which prompt is an example of zero-shot prompting?
options: “Here are two examples of formal emails. Write a third in the same style.”
“Think through each step, then give the answer.”
“Write the prompt that would produce this paragraph.”
items.why: A zero-shot prompt asks for the task directly, without examples. The first option is few-shot, the second is chain-of-thought, and the third is reverse prompting.

items.stem: A student asks an AI to outline an essay, then asks it to write the first paragraph from that outline, then the second paragraph. Which technique is this?
items.why: Prompt chaining breaks a task into steps, with each prompt building on the output of the one before.

items.stem: Which prompt transforms content into a different media type?
options: “Fix the spelling and grammar in this report.”
“Create an infographic image that shows these five statistics.”
items.why: Turning text data into an image changes the media type. The other prompts keep the content as text.

items.stem: An AI tool says 34% of U.S. households have a smart speaker. Which TWO steps best verify this number? (Choose two.)
options: Ask the AI to repeat the answer
Find the original survey or dataset and confirm the figure and its date
Accept it because it is a specific percentage
Compare it with another reliable, recent source
items.why: Check numbers against the original source and a second reliable source, and look at the date. A specific-sounding number can still be made up or out of date.

items.stem: Which Responsible AI principle says that people, not the AI system, must be answerable for the system's decisions and outcomes?
items.why: Accountability means a named person or team is responsible for how an AI system is designed, deployed and used.

items.stem: Which capability turns written text into natural-sounding spoken audio?
options: Text to speech in Azure Speech
items.why: Text to speech (speech synthesis) creates spoken audio from text. OCR does the reverse for images: it reads text out of them.

items.stem: Which TWO tasks can Azure AI Vision perform? (Choose two.)
options: Detect the sentiment of a product review
Read printed and handwritten text in an image
Translate a phone call in real time
Generate tags and a caption that describe an image
items.why: Vision analyzes images: OCR, tags, captions, objects. Sentiment belongs to Azure AI Language, and live call translation to Azure Speech.

items.stem: Why do you hold back a test set that the model never sees during training?
options: To estimate how the model will perform on new, unseen data
To give the model more examples to memorize
To remove outliers from the data
items.why: A held-out test set shows how well the model generalizes. Testing on the training data would overstate its accuracy.

items.stem: Which classification metric combines precision and recall into a single number?
items.why: The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall. MAE and R² are regression metrics, and the learning rate is a training setting.

items.stem: After deployment, a model's predictions get a little worse every month. What should the team put in place first?
options: Monitoring that tracks performance and data drift, with alerts and a retraining plan
A larger test set from the original training data
items.why: Production models need ongoing monitoring so drift is caught and the model is retrained before it causes harm.
